prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1275; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received from the policyholder reporting a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The insured vehicle's right rear quarter panel and mirror housing show damage consistent with the reported contact.

Entry 2: Policyholder's household member was driving at the time of loss and is covered as a household member under the policy. Coverage was in force on the date of loss, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report obtained, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the lane change as the reported cause. Responding officer's notes match the parties' initial statements.

Entry 4: Photographs submitted by the insured show the vehicle damage in detail and confirm several scene features described in the first statement. No independent witnesses have come forward to date.

Entry 5: Claimant's counsel has written to advise that the claimant is represented and requests that all further contact go through the firm. Direct contact with the claimant has been stopped accordingly.

Entry 6: Claimant reports neck and upper back pain with whiplash-type symptoms following the impact. It is not yet clear whether the reported injury came from this crash, and medical records are being requested.

Entry 7: Inspection of the insured vehicle completed. Damage pattern matches the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 8: Claimant's medical file received. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records provided, and the treating provider notes a usual course of care following the reported event.

Entry 9: Claimant's counsel forwarded a revised statement adding minor details about the lane change and the vehicle's speed. The core account is unchanged from the initial report.

Entry 10: Treatment records show physiotherapy that followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved. Treating provider notes reduced symptom reports over the most recent visits.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file with the claims supervisor. The vehicle damage supports the reported mechanism, and the injury question remains open pending the medical review requested from the independent examiner.

Entry 12: File status updated to awaiting the independent medical review and the counsel's damages package. Reserve held at current level until the injury causation question is resolved.
